title: RoadMaper — AI-Powered Learning Roadmap Platform
tagline: Independently designed, built, and shipped a full-stack AI product end-to-end using AI-assisted "vibe coding" — proof of using AI efficiently to reach a working, problem-solved outcome, not just a prompt.
problem: Anyone learning a new skill or preparing for an exam faces the same wall: too many resources, no clear sequence, and no accountability system to actually finish. I wanted to prove that AI tools (Claude, Cursor AI) can be used not just to autocomplete code, but to take a product from idea to a real, working, deployable app.
approach: Built a full-stack Next.js 15 app (TypeScript, PostgreSQL, Prisma, NextAuth) where a user describes any goal in free text; an LLM (Groq Llama-3.3-70B) classifies the goal and generates a personalized day-by-day or phase-based roadmap, persisted as structured tasks and projects. Layered in Google/GitHub OAuth, a daily task tracker with streaks, browser push reminders, an AI "self-learn" insights engine, and auto-generated completion reports across 26 API routes. The AI generated the scaffolding — I owned the architecture, debugged auth/session issues, fixed type and lint errors across the codebase, and made the product-design calls that turned a prototype into something that actually ships.
impact: Went from a free-text goal to a working product a real user can sign in to, get a personalized plan from, and track daily — demonstrating the ability to use AI as a force-multiplier while still owning the engineering and problem-solving that AI alone doesn't finish.

title: World & India CO₂ Emissions — Smart Life Environmental Impact Analytics
tagline: Why our smart living impacts the world: 24 years of global CO₂ data, decoded into what's actually driving India's footprint.
problem: Climate data is usually reported as abstract global totals that don't connect to daily life. I wanted to answer a more personal question: how much does everyday "smart living" — smart TVs, fridges, routers, streaming — actually contribute to India's emissions, and where should policy focus first?
approach: Analyzed 24 years (2000-2024) of global CO2 emissions across 190+ countries (OWID dataset) in Python, then built a companion "Smart Life" model estimating device-level energy use and CO2 output using IEA benchmarks and India's grid emission factor. Delivered two linked dashboards in Python and Power BI covering source-wise emissions (coal/oil/gas), the top-10 global emitters, per-capita trend lines, a state-wise environmental impact heatmap, and 2030 policy-impact projections.

metrics.label: CO2 cut linked to higher awareness

impact: India's emissions are up 19.6% since 2020 to 8.27% of the global share - yet its per-capita footprint sits 47% below the world average. Ranked policy interventions by estimated CO2 reduction (EV + solar subsidies ~30%, real-time energy dashboards ~21%, smart meters ~18%) to turn the analysis into actionable recommendations.
